paragraphs: SQLite official documentation: “Write-Ahead Logging” (https://sqlite.org/wal.html), section “1. Overview,” under “Disadvantages.” It states: “All processes using a database must be on the same host computer; WAL does not work over a network filesystem.” The stated reason is: “WAL requires all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.” Thus, clients on different machines cannot use WAL for a shared database over a network filesystem because WAL requires shared memory among all participating processes.

SQLite’s official reason is that WAL requires all processes using the database to share a small amount of memory. Processes on different host machines cannot share that memory, so SQLite requires WAL participants to be on the same host; consequently, WAL does not work when clients share a database through a network filesystem. This is the documented mechanism and limitation, not an inference beyond the documentation. Source: https://sqlite.org/wal.html
